propositions.name: distinct_present_past_future
propositions.statement: We distinguish present sensation from the remembrance of past sensations and the anticipation of future sensations.
propositions.quote: we distinguish without difficulty present sensation from the remembrance of past sensations or the anticipation of future sensations

propositions.name: conscious_phenomena_ordered
propositions.statement: Of two conscious phenomena which we remember, one was anterior to the other.
propositions.quote: we know perfectly well what we mean when we say that of two conscious phenomena which we remember, one was anterior to the other

propositions.name: simultaneity_as_interpenetration
propositions.statement: Two conscious facts are simultaneous when they profoundly interpenetrate, so that analysis can not separate them without mutilating them.
propositions.quote: When we say that two conscious facts are simultaneous, we mean that they profoundly interpenetrate, so that analysis can not separate them without mutilating them.

propositions.name: order_of_conscious_phenomena_imposed
propositions.statement: The order in which we arrange conscious phenomena does not admit of any arbitrariness; it is imposed upon us.
propositions.quote: The order in which we arrange conscious phenomena does not admit of any arbitrariness. It is imposed upon us and of it we can change nothing.

propositions.name: memory_requires_ceasing_to_be_actual
propositions.statement: For a sensation to become a remembrance, it must have ceased to be actual and lost the sense of its infinite complexity, otherwise it would have remained present.
propositions.quote: it must have ceased to be actual, we must have lost the sense of its infinite complexity, otherwise it would have remained present

propositions.name: labels_finite_time_discontinuous
propositions.statement: These labels can only be finite in number, so psychologic time should be discontinuous.
propositions.quote: these labels can only be finite in number. On that score, psychologic time should be discontinuous.

propositions.name: time_pre_existent_form_of_mind
propositions.statement: Time is a form pre-existent in our minds.
propositions.quote: How could that be, if time were not a form pre-existent in our minds?

propositions.name: physical_facts_unseen_by_consciousness
propositions.statement: Physical facts are those with which we people space and which no consciousness sees directly.
propositions.quote: we wish to put there physical facts, these I know not what with which we people space and which no consciousness sees directly

propositions.name: psychologic_time_qualitative
propositions.statement: Psychologic time is qualitative, and we ask whether we can transform it into a quantitative time.
propositions.quote: Can we transform psychologic time, which is qualitative, into a quantitative time?

propositions.name: no_direct_intuition_equality_of_durations
propositions.statement: We have not a direct intuition of the equality of two intervals of time.
propositions.quote: We have not a direct intuition of the equality of two intervals of time .

propositions.name: pendulum_beats_assumed_equal
propositions.statement: To measure time, physicists and astronomers use the pendulum and suppose that all the beats of this pendulum are of equal duration.
propositions.quote: To measure time they use the pendulum and they suppose by definition that all the beats of this pendulum are of equal duration.

propositions.name: pendulum_perturbed_by_physical_causes
propositions.statement: The temperature, the resistance of the air, the barometric pressure, and other causes such as electric or magnetic perturbations make the pace of the pendulum vary.
propositions.quote: the temperature, the resistance of the air, the barometric pressure, make the pace of the pendulum vary

propositions.name: sidereal_day_constant_unit
propositions.statement: The sidereal day, the duration of the rotation of the earth, is the constant unit of time, and two complete rotations of the earth are supposed to have the same duration.
propositions.quote: it is the sidereal day, that is, the duration of the rotation of the earth, which is the constant unit of time

propositions.name: earth_rotation_slowing
propositions.statement: The tides act as a check on the globe, and the rotation of the earth is becoming slower and slower.
propositions.quote: the tides act as a check on our globe, and that the rotation of the earth is becoming slower and slower

propositions.name: moon_apparent_acceleration_explained_by_earth_slowing
propositions.statement: The apparent acceleration of the motion of the moon is explained because our watch, which is the earth, is going slow.
propositions.quote: Thus would be explained the apparent acceleration of the motion of the moon, which would seem to be going more rapidly than theory permits because our watch, which is the earth, is going slow.

propositions.name: postulate_same_causes_same_time
propositions.statement: The duration of two identical phenomena is the same: the same causes take the same time to produce the same effects.
propositions.quote: It is that the duration of two identical phenomena is the same; or, if you prefer, that the same causes take the same time to produce the same effects.

propositions.name: postulate_could_be_contradicted_by_experiment
propositions.statement: It is not impossible that experiment may some day contradict this postulate.
propositions.quote: Is it impossible that experiment may some day contradict our postulate?

propositions.name: multitude_of_causes_produce_effect
propositions.statement: In physical reality one cause does not produce a given effect, but a multitude of distinct causes contribute to produce it.
propositions.quote: In physical reality one cause does not produce a given effect, but a multitude of distinct causes contribute to produce it, without our having any means of discriminating the part of each of them.

propositions.name: causes_never_reproduced_exactly
propositions.statement: Causes almost identical take almost the same time to produce almost the same effects, since the causes which have produced an effect will never be reproduced except approximately.
propositions.quote: Instead of saying: ‘The same causes take the same time to produce the same effects,’ we should say: ‘Causes almost identical take almost the same time to produce almost the same effects.’

propositions.name: tidal_friction_destroys_vis_viva
propositions.statement: The friction of the tides producing heat must destroy vis viva, by the principle of vis viva, or of the conservation of energy.
propositions.quote: They say first that the friction of the tides producing heat must destroy vis viva . They invoke therefore the principle of vis viva , or of the conservation of energy.

propositions.name: newtons_law_used_for_moon_acceleration
propositions.statement: The secular acceleration of the moon, calculated according to Newton's law, would be less than that deduced from observations unless the correction for the slowing down of the terrestrial rotation is made.
propositions.quote: They say next that the secular acceleration of the moon, calculated according to Newton’s law, would be less than that deduced from observations unless the correction relative to the slowing down of the terrestrial rotation were made.

propositions.name: newtons_law_approximate_experimental_truth
propositions.statement: Newton's law is an experimental truth, and as such it is only approximate.
propositions.quote: Newton’s law is an experimental truth; as such it is only approximate, which shows that we still have only a definition by approximation.

propositions.name: time_defined_for_simplicity_of_mechanics
propositions.statement: There is not one way of measuring time more true than another; that which is generally adopted is only more convenient.
propositions.quote: In other words, there is not one way of measuring time more true than another; that which is generally adopted is only more convenient .

propositions.name: star_light_takes_time_to_reach_earth
propositions.statement: At least two hundred years were necessary for the light from that star to reach our earth.
propositions.quote: at least two hundred years were necessary for the light from that star to reach our earth

propositions.name: relating_physical_and_psychological_phenomena_needs_convention
propositions.statement: These affirmations have by themselves no meaning; they can have meaning only as the outcome of a convention.
propositions.quote: A little reflection is sufficient to understand that all these affirmations have by themselves no meaning. They can have one only as the outcome of a convention.

propositions.name: physical_facts_succession_not_invertible_at_will
propositions.statement: This definition would not suit two physical facts which happen far from one another; we no longer understand what this reversibility would be.
propositions.quote: It is evident that this definition would not suit two physical facts which happen far from one another, and that, in what concerns them, we no longer even understand what this reversibility would be

propositions.name: cause_defines_anteriority
propositions.statement: When a phenomenon appears to us as the cause of another, we regard it as anterior; it is by cause that we define time.
propositions.quote: when a phenomenon appears to us as the cause of another, we regard it as anterior. It is therefore by cause that we define time

propositions.name: antecedent_assumed_cause_of_consequent
propositions.statement: We assume that the anterior fact, the antecedent, is the cause of the other, the consequent; it is by time that we define cause.
propositions.quote: We assume that the anterior fact, the antecedent, is the cause of the other, of the consequent. It is then by time that we define cause.

propositions.name: thunder_caused_by_electric_discharge
propositions.statement: I hear thunder, and I conclude there has been an electric discharge; I consider the physical phenomenon as anterior to the auditory image, because I believe it is its cause.
propositions.quote: I hear thunder, and I conclude there has been an electric discharge; I do not hesitate to consider the physical phenomenon as anterior to the auditory image perceived in my consciousness, because I believe it is its cause.

propositions.name: sound_of_thunder_delayed_after_discharge
propositions.statement: We hear the sound of the thunder only some seconds after the electric discharge of the cloud.
propositions.quote: We hear the sound of the thunder only some seconds after the electric discharge of the cloud.

propositions.name: distant_lightning_flash_can_precede_near_one_despite_later_sound
propositions.statement: Of two flashes of lightning, the one distant, the other near, the first can be anterior to the second, even though the sound of the second comes to us before that of the first.
propositions.quote: can not the first be anterior to the second, even though the sound of the second comes to us before that of the first?

propositions.name: universe_causally_interchained
propositions.statement: If all the parts of the universe are interchained, any one phenomenon is not the effect of a single cause, but the resultant of causes infinitely numerous.
propositions.quote: If all the parts of the universe are interchained in a certain measure, any one phenomenon will not be the effect of a single cause, but the resultant of causes infinitely numerous

propositions.name: positions_velocities_determine_future_and_past
propositions.statement: The positions and the velocities of three bodies at a given instant suffice to determine their positions and velocities at the following instant, and at any instant.
propositions.quote: The positions and the velocities of three bodies at a given instant suffice to determine their positions and velocities at the following instant, and consequently at any instant.

propositions.name: positions_of_bodies_governed_by_precise_laws
propositions.statement: Positions occupied by bodies at different instants are bound to one another by laws as precise as that of Newton, though more complicated.
propositions.quote: by laws as precise as that of Newton, though more complicated. Then why not regard one of these aggregates as the cause of the other, which would lead to considering as simultaneous the instant

propositions.name: velocity_of_light_constant_postulate
propositions.statement: Light has a constant velocity, and its velocity is the same in all directions; this postulate is necessary for any measurement of this velocity.
propositions.quote: He has begun by supposing that light has a constant velocity, and in particular that its velocity is the same in all directions.

propositions.name: velocity_of_light_postulate_unverifiable_directly
propositions.statement: This postulate could never be verified directly by experiment; it might be contradicted if the results of different measurements were not concordant.
propositions.quote: This postulate could never be verified directly by experiment; it might be contradicted by it if the results of different measurements were not concordant.

propositions.name: roemer_measured_light_velocity_via_jupiter_eclipses
propositions.statement: Roemer used eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter, and sought how much the event fell behind its prediction, to measure the velocity of light.
propositions.quote: You know that Roemer used eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter, and sought how much the event fell behind its prediction.

propositions.name: moon_eclipse_not_simultaneous_everywhere_due_to_light_propagation
propositions.statement: An eclipse of the moon is not perceived simultaneously from all points of the earth, since the propagation of light is not instantaneous.
propositions.quote: they suppose that this phenomenon is perceived simultaneously from all points of the earth. That is not altogether true, since the propagation of light is not instantaneous

propositions.name: telegraph_signal_reception_after_sending
propositions.statement: The reception of the signal at Berlin is after the sending of this same signal from Paris.
propositions.quote: It is clear first that the reception of the signal at Berlin, for instance, is after the sending of this same signal from Paris.

propositions.name: rules_chosen_for_convenience_not_truth
propositions.statement: We choose these rules, not because they are true, but because they are the most convenient.
propositions.quote: We therefore choose these rules, not because they are true, but because they are the most convenient
